notes.fact_check: 2026-09-27 AMBER: Science Advances, 9 Sept 2026, DOI 10.1126/sciadv.aei1901. Griffith University (Adam Brumm) with Roger Papke (University of Florida). n = 2 skeletons; one ~7,000 years, the other 16,000-25,000. Say "up to 25,000", "may be the earliest". Betel: fourth most widely used psychoactive substance; "getting high" overstates a mild stimulant.

end.title: One verified science story a day

caption:
Two forager skeletons from Sulawesi show a novel tooth-wear pattern and traces of arecoline, from betel nut, today the fourth most used psychoactive substance. Griffith University (Adam Brumm). Science Advances, 9 Sept 2026. Caveats: n = 2; the older skeleton is dated 16,000 to 25,000 years, and headlines quote the top. The authors say it may be the earliest evidence of drug use.

#archaeology #anthropology #science #history
voiceover_script: The headline says humans got high twenty five thousand years ago. Here is what is actually behind it. Two forager skeletons from Sulawesi, in Indonesia. Two. That is the whole sample. Their teeth show a wear pattern nobody had described before, plus chemical traces of arecoline, which comes from betel nut, today the world's fourth most used psychoactive substance, a mild stimulant. Now the date. The older skeleton is dated somewhere between sixteen thousand and twenty five thousand years. The headlines quote the top of that range. Even so, the authors say it may be the earliest evidence of drug use found so far. Griffith University, Science Advances, ninth of September. Source in the caption.
